recipes.name: All-American Trifle
ingredients_raw: 3 pounds fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
1 (3.3 ounce) package instant white chocolate pudding mix
2 tablespoons coconut-flavored rum, or to taste, divided
2 pints fresh blueberries, or as needed

steps.text: Sprinkle strawberries with sugar in a bowl; stir to distribute sugar, and set aside.
Chill a large metal mixing bowl and beaters from an electric mixer.
Pour cream into the chilled mixing bowl, and add lemon yogurt, pudding mix, and about 1 tablespoon of coconut rum; beat until fluffy with an electric mixer set on medium speed.

Spread a layer of pound cake cubes into the bottom of a glass trifle dish, and sprinkle cubes with remaining tablespoon coconut rum. Cover pound cake with a layer of strawberries; sprinkle blueberries over strawberries. Spread a thick layer of whipped cream over the berries.

Repeat the layers several times, ending with a layer of strawberries sprinkled with blueberries and reserving about 1 cup of whipped cream; top the trifle with dollops of whipped cream to serve. Refrigerate leftovers.

raw_recipe.headline: All-American Trifle
raw_recipe.description: This red white and blue Fourth of July trifle is made by layering pound cake, whipped cream, strawberries, and blueberries for the perfect celebratory dessert.

review.reviewBody: I made this for 4th of July, and it was a HUGE hit! It was easy, served a large crowd, and had people begging for seconds! Looks like something you spent a lot of time and effort on, but was really quick, easy, and delicious!

This was a big hit for our 4th of July dessert! I did use 4lbs of strawberries and 4 pints of blueberries. We like fruit! I’ll definitely make this again! I’ll add an extra pint of cream next time. We’re a large family. Also, I put the 2 TBSP of coconut rum in the cream. No one knew there was rum but it did andd more depth to the flavors. Everyone loved it, adults and kids! Comments were: delicious, fresh, light and seconds, please! Bonus: it’s beautiful!

I made this for 4th of July and it got great reviews from everyone. I also found that the full recipe made a lot of dessert - but then I did double the cream as others suggested. I used a 12 cup bowl and I had enough to make 1 1/2 bowls. The only thing I would change the next time is to add more lemon to the cream - perhaps it was my brand of yogurt but it wasn't as strong of a lemon flavor as I would have liked.

Absolutely delicious! Would make again. My diabetic mom was over for July 4th so I cut the sugar out from the strawberries. They are sweet enough anyway. I also used no sugar instant pudding and less sugar for the lemon yogurt. Couldn't find low sugar or no sugar pound cake so I just used what I could purchase. My Mom absolutely loved it and yes, I did add the Coconut Rum. Only 3 Tablespoons. Okay swap out for eliminating the other 3 ingredients for sugar.

Huge hit! As a tip, I’d cut the strawberries in small cubes. The moisture seems to come from the strawberries. As they give off their liquid the remaining fruit loses its color and gets a mooshy texture. Larger slices call attention to this. 

I do like topping the cake with large slices. (Don’t use my trifle as your example to aspire to!). However, I’d try to figure out a clear sugar glaze to better preserve the look of the strawberries.

As my cut strawberries sat coated in sugar in a bowl waiting to be added to the trifle, they were already releasing liquid. I poured this liquid over the top of the trifle when I was done with the layers.

I did use cheesecake flavored pudding mix because white chocolate wasn’t available. I’m sure it’s good either way.

Finally, I used food coloring in my cake layers to make more festive.

I made this for a BBQ this summer. It was a big hit. The only thing I changed was the presentation of how I served it. I used small cups and made individual servings and that was a huge hit! Also because I had children at the cookout I omitted the rum! Will definitely make again!!

I make this every 4th of July and my family loves it! I follow the recipe exactly (minus the rum) I always forget that I would want to add an extra 1/4 cup of cream to have just a little extra moose for the recipe, but that’s just me. The recipe makes just enough, I just make my layers thick! I also get 4 lbs strawberries and 3 pints blueberries so that I have plenty to toss in each layer.

Made this for 4th of July party and everyone loved it - kids and adults! I had more than enough ingredients to make two trifles, so this recipe probably was meant to fit a large trifle bowl - like those cake platters that turn upside down. Next time I'll use just one pound cake, 2 pounds strawberries and 3C of cream to fit my smaller bowl. I also think I'll try coconut yogurt and drizzle both layers of cake with rum for added flavor. And there will be a next time! This was a fun recipe to make together with my 10yo daughter.

After reading the comments saying it "makes a lot" I put it in a punch bowl. You can see how high it came in my photo.

I also used whipping cream instead of heavy cream and boy-oh-boy did it thicken up quick! Probably could have used the heavy cream like the recipe says.

How did it turn out? GREAT! The whole thing was devoured and I will definitely make it again for the next 4th-of-July!

This is one of the easiest desserts I've ever made. I made it for Christmas Eve dessert and was delighted with the results. I varied from this recipe, but this was a great starting point!The store was out of strawberries so I used raspberries as a substitute, mixing them in 1/4 cup sugar. I also kept the blueberries; personally I don'tlike blueberries, however I think they are nice, fresh addition to this dessert.I decided to simplify the pudding so I used a 5.1 oz vanilla pudding mix, with 3 cups of cold milk. Whisk for two minutes, let sit for five. It was delicious!I used pound cake. I also excluded the coconut rum.My Trifle bowl is 5½-6 inches deep. The measurements in this recipe were over-kill for sure, although I can't give it all the blame seeing as I didn't follow it completely. It calls for 3 lbs of strawberries so I bought 3 lbs of raspberries, but that was too much; i bought two pound cakes, as it called for, and there's still about half a cake left over; WAY too many blueberries; I could also only fit in one layer of pudding because my bowl was too full, which is sad because the pudding is such a great part of this dessert! In the end I made a second, smaller trifle to use up some of the leftovers.All in all though this was a great recipe for a first time trifle maker to use! I really appreciate having this recipe to use as a foundation. The trifle was delicious and looked beautiful, so thank you so much for this recipe! Sometime in summer I'll have to try it with strawberries and the lemon yogurt pudding!!

This was a definite hit! Of course, I made a few adjustments. I used kiwi and strawberries for the fruit and just one pound cake. I used Truwhip (no high fructose) instead of whipping cream and Rum extract, not Rum. This was yummy and true crowd pleaser. I will certainly make this again with other fruit possibly.
I made this for a graduation party and everyone loved it! So easy to put together! A must try!
Love the recipe but I find the pound cake density to be a little overwhelming. Personally I prefer to use an angel food cake as it’s “softer” and more porous.
So delicious and easy to make! Everyone enjoyed it!
I used banana instant pudding mix instead of white chocolate and oh my goodness was it amazing! Definitely a winner!!
I made this with my 5 year old daughter for the Fourth of July. It was sooo good. We left out the rum, and added vanilla extract instead. Very delicious .
Very delicious!
Enjoyed making it did not change one thing family loved it

Red, white and blue ! What an awesome shortcake to serve at celebrations. The fresh strawberries and blueberries are so easy on the eyes and the soft pound cake makes it a crowd pleaser. I followed the directions and the trifle came together quite quickly. A lot of my guests came back for seconds.

Absolutely wonderful. Came together easily with pound cake from the bakery, and I cheated and used Cool Whip rather than making my own cream and it was just fine. Also used coconut flavoring instead of rum. Not sure what it is about these flavor combinations, but it truly is delicious!
